narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance emerged in the early 2000s at the Metropolis nightclub in Rungis, France, through parties organized by Cyril Blanc and Alexandre Barouzdin.
The brand 'Tecktonik' was registered as a trademark in 2002 to control the commercial use of the name and associated merchandise.
on_screen: Map: France · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally performed in clubs like Metropolis, the dance also spread through street gatherings called 'aprems' and became a significant early example of a viral internet dance phenomenon.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Freestyle Dance Styles - EDM ( DnB Step, Electro Shuffle, Tectonic). (https://archive.org/details/dance-stylez-edm-dn-b-step-electro-shuffle-tecktonik)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The style emphasizes rapid, geometric arm movements, often incorporating glowsticking techniques like the figure eight.
Footwork is rhythmic and fluid, featuring shuffles and toprock elements performed in time with the music.
Watch for Figure Eight, Leading Hand.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (e4MM2lxrnBw)

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Tecktonik is performed to fast-paced electro house and techno music, often imported from Northern Europe, including hardstyle and jumpstyle genres.
Listen for the electronic synthesizers, drum machines.
The pulse is 4/4.
Fast-paced, high-energy electronic music characterized by repetitive, driving beats and synthesized melodies typical of early 2000s European club culture.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Cyril Blanc and Alexandre Barouzdin are the primary figures behind the Tecktonik brand and event series.
In Brazil, the dance was popularized in the late 2000s and early 2010s, with organized groups and events like 'Vertifight' held in cities like São Paulo.
The style is a synthesis of industrial dance, Moroccan chaabi, disco, vogue, waacking, hip-hop, and freehand glowsticking.
